stories.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after Trump intervention
stories.summary: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after President Trump said he 'convinced' the board to bring him back, a move that has drawn backlash. Huang's comeback helped add about $1tn to the company's stock value. The FT reports Trump made up to $15mn on Nvidia shares after the return, based on the maximum amount he could have owned in the latest disclosure.

stories.headline: Ukraine says it sank Russian warship off Libya
stories.summary: Ukraine says it used seven naval drones launched from a mothership to strike two Russian vessels off Libya on Sunday. One of the strikes sank the corvette Merkury, one of Russia's newest vessels. Zelenskyy hailed the attack, and the BBC's Frank Gardner says it raises the stakes of the war.

stories.headline: Russian nuclear satellite reports prompt Nato response
stories.summary: Nato's chief has vowed defence against a space threat after German media reported Russia plans to launch a satellite carrying a nuclear warhead into space in the coming weeks. The report comes as Russian incursions into Nato territory increase, after three Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland on Friday.

stories.headline: Democrats win House by widest margin in 50 years
stories.summary: Democrats have flipped 47 House seats so far and could reach 49 in total, the largest House margin for the party in 50 years. The result is a major political story in the US.

stories.headline: UN climate talks COP31 end with no deal
stories.summary: The COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, ended with no agreement after running two days longer than planned, making it the longest UN climate conference in history. Australia, which co-hosted, blamed 'difficult geopolitical times', while carbon capture and removal emerged as a dividing line.

stories.headline: Myanmar genocide ruling prompts sanctions and migrant returns
stories.summary: The UK has sanctioned top Myanmar military leaders, joining other nations in recognising an ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. Malaysia says it will send thousands of migrants and refugees back to Myanmar, despite acknowledging junta 'atrocities'.

stories.headline: Markets rally as Nvidia's comeback lifts AI trade
stories.summary: US stocks had their best day in more than a year on Monday after Huang's return revived AI enthusiasm. The tech-heavy Nasdaq rose 6.5%, and Nvidia logged its biggest one-day gain in stock-market history, with its shares up more than 30%. Asian and emerging-market stocks also rallied, though copper gave back its gains.

stories.headline: US blacklists Megaspeed over chip diversion concerns
stories.summary: The US has added Asian AI firm Megaspeed and six other companies to its trade blacklist over concerns about diversion of advanced computing products. Megaspeed has been accused of funnelling AI chips to China, linked to a former executive's affair with Jensen Huang becoming public.

stories.headline: Capita shares plunge 70% as chief executive quits
stories.summary: Capita's shares fell 70% after chief executive Adolfo Hernandez left with immediate effect, admitting the group 'has not delivered' for retired civil servants waiting for pension payments. The scheme has been overseen by Capita since last year.

stories.headline: Compass plans US stock market switch
stories.summary: Compass, the £43.6bn NHS caterer and one of the FTSE 100's biggest companies, is planning to move its primary listing from London to New York. The move would be the latest blow to the UK stock market.

stories.headline: Poundland faces possible collapse
stories.summary: Poundland has a matter of days to find a buyer or face collapsing into administration. Next has also warned that hackers accessed data via a third-party technology supplier, though it says no personal data that could lead to fraud was accessed.

stories.headline: Brentford beat 10-man Everton 3-0
stories.summary: Brentford beat Everton 3-0 in the Premier League after James Tarkowski was sent off for his first Premier League red card. Vitaly Janelt scored a stunner, and the result handed David Moyes a painful 593rd game in charge of Everton. Everton had lost 4-0 at Brentford in an earlier report.

stories.headline: Penge wins RSM Classic in playoff
stories.summary: England's Marco Penge won his first PGA Tour title by birdying the first extra hole in a four-man play-off at the RSM Classic in Georgia. The win secures his PGA Tour card for 2027.

stories.headline: Arsenal face Dortmund in Champions League
stories.summary: English champions Arsenal face German league leaders Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday. Predictions and lineups are available.

stories.headline: England and Ireland impress in autumn rugby
stories.summary: Ireland's Andy Farrell says the victory over South Africa 'sets us up nicely' for next year's World Cup. England's Tommy Freeman is in contention for Saturday's Nations Championship play-off against New Zealand, after England beat the All Blacks 37-12. New Zealand Rugby has backed coach Dave Rennie despite two bad losses.

stories.headline: Priyansh Arya hits 181 in T20
stories.summary: Delhi captain Priyansh Arya smashed 181 against Tamil Nadu in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, the second-highest score in T20 history, hitting 19 sixes. Steve Smith made a laboured 12 for NSW against Queensland in his Sheffield Shield comeback.

stories.headline: Carbon removal and capture divides deepen after COP31
stories.summary: Carbon capture and removal were fault lines at COP31, which ended without a deal. Carbon Herald reports the Storegga stake in the Acorn CCS project was sold to EnEarth, and the UK East Coast Cluster has awarded over £2.25bn in supply chain contracts.

stories.headline: Nigeria and Rwanda carbon removal deals
stories.summary: VP Capital has invested in Nigeria-based AirSmat's biochar carbon removal, and Removall Carbon has partnered with a Rwandan firm on an agroforestry project. EDF Trading has also signed to supply CORSIA-compliant credits to airlines through 2035.

stories.headline: GTA 6 hacker released on licence
stories.summary: Arion Kurtaj, 21, pleaded guilty to the Rockstar Games hack and others he carried out as a teenager. He has been released on licence with a warning 'don't let this happen again'.

stories.headline: Gisèle Pelicot nude photos sent to media
stories.summary: Gisèle Pelicot said she was 'humiliated' after nude photos were sent to media to promote a book, according to the BBC. The publisher of an essay on coercive control has apologised for 'an unfortunate and inappropriate communication'.

stories.headline: Co-op Live Manchester evacuation probed
stories.summary: Police are investigating an unknown substance that caused an evacuation at Manchester's Co-op Live arena during a Don Toliver gig. Rapper Don Toliver has postponed two arena shows, and concertgoers criticised the lack of security.

stories.headline: You Can See Everything passes $100m
stories.summary: Nathan Fielder's documentary about Elizabeth Holmes has passed $100m at the global box office, with a record UK opening weekend. Ariana Grande joins Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro in Focker In-Law, which one review calls a tired fourth outing.

stories.headline: Spielberg to make Paul Thomas Anderson western
stories.summary: Steven Spielberg is making a western scripted by Paul Thomas Anderson, based on Kevin's novel The Heart in Winter. Jessie Buckley, Cillian Murphy and Mark Rylance will reportedly star, according to Deadline.

stories.headline: Volunteer finds lost toddler in Arizona desert
stories.summary: A volunteer, Jay Stewart, found a missing toddler in the cold desert at night and has been honoured by the sheriff's office as an outstanding citizen. He said he felt what everyone else searching felt.

stories.headline: Alaska walrus habitat protected forever
stories.summary: Conservationists have secured permanent protection for barrier islands off Alaska's Bering Sea coast, home to the largest concentrations of Pacific walrus in North America, around 200,000 animals. The refuge sits near the village of Point Lay.

stories.headline: Veteran's son thanks 33 schoolchildren
stories.summary: In 1967, 33 Massachusetts schoolchildren wrote letters to a wounded Navy corpsman in Vietnam. Almost 60 years later, his son is searching for them to say thank you.

stories.headline: Pontevedra's car-free push
stories.summary: The Spanish city of Pontevedra kicked out cars before it was fashionable, a shift that has left even local taxi drivers reflecting on change. The story looks at how the city reshaped its streets.

stories.headline: Why AI conquered chess but humans still matter
stories.summary: Ahead of the world chess championship between 20-year-olds Javokhir Sindarov and Gukesh Dommaraju in Geneva, a Guardian piece argues that AI's conquest of chess offers a surprising lesson about what AI cannot replicate.
